text: At 90+2', Harbour City increased their pressing intensity from 0.6 to 0.78 and raised their defensive line height from 0.62 to 0.74, simultaneously boosting directness from 0.28 to 0.43 to chase a one-goal deficit [#1884]. This pressing trigger aimed to disrupt Seabrook Town’s wide, crossing-oriented buildup characteristic of their 3-4-3 formation by forcing turnovers higher upfield and facilitating quicker progression or direct balls into the final third [#1884],. Although possession for Harbour City rose from 31.7% to 40.8%, Seabrook Town’s xG increased from 0.55 to 0.99, reflecting the transition risk of exposing space behind the higher defensive line [#1884]. The partial field tilt (38.1% for Harbour City, 61.9% for Seabrook) alongside a PPDA of 6.2 for Harbour City versus 4.5 for Seabrook Town in the last 10 minutes indicates that this aggressive pressing was reactive and insufficient to overturn Seabrook Town’s control in the critical closing moments.
